# Documentation

> As a self-service engineering platform, Meshery enables collaborative design and operation of cloud native infrastructure.


## Pages
- [Meshery Documentation](/index.md)
- [Search Results](/search/index.md)

## Installation
- [Installation](/installation/index.md): Choose where to run Meshery, on Kubernetes or a Docker host, and find the installation guide for your platform.

- [Overview](/installation/overview/index.md): Meshery is the self-service engineering platform, enabling collaborative design and operation of cloud and cloud native infrastructure.
- [Quick Start Guide](/installation/quick-start/index.md): Install mesheryctl and start Meshery on a Kubernetes cluster or a Docker host with a single command, then connect your clusters and start designing.
- [Using Meshery Playground](/installation/playground/index.md): Try Meshery in your browser, connected to live Kubernetes clusters, without installing anything.
- [Deployment Models & Reference Architecture](/installation/production/deployment-models/index.md): In-cluster vs. out-of-cluster, Docker vs. Kubernetes, the Meshery component inventory and its statefulness, and the topology patterns for single-cluster, multi-cluster, and multi-cloud production deployments.
- [Infrastructure, Sizing & Performance](/installation/production/infrastructure-sizing-and-performance/index.md): Resource requirements per Meshery component, capacity planning, MeshSync tiered discovery, Broker throughput, scalability levers, and the known performance bounds to plan around in production.
- [High Availability & Resiliency](/installation/production/high-availability-and-resiliency/index.md): Replication, health probes, failure modes and recovery, the ephemeral database, Remote Provider persistence, and backup & disaster-recovery posture for resilient Meshery operation.
- [Upgrading Meshery](/installation/upgrades/index.md): How Meshery's components version together, and the step-by-step procedure for upgrading the CLI, Server, Operator, MeshSync, and Broker on Docker and Kubernetes deployments.
- [Networking & Connectivity](/installation/production/networking-and-connectivity/index.md): Network ports and directional flows, ingress and Emissary configuration, secure WebSocket support, CDN and edge caching of the UI, Broker exposure, egress to Remote Providers, the OAuth callback URL, and network policies for production Meshery.
- [Security Hardening](/installation/production/security-hardening/index.md): RBAC and least privilege, pod and container security contexts, secret and kubeconfig handling, TLS, supply-chain integrity, Broker exposure risk, namespace isolation, and extension trust for hardening Meshery in production.
- [Authentication, Authorization & Identity](/installation/production/authentication-and-identity/index.md): Why to preselect a Remote Provider over the Local Provider, OAuth callback configuration, identity providers, capabilities, and keys/permissions for production Meshery.
- [Multi-Cluster & Multi-Cloud Operations](/installation/production/multi-cluster-and-multi-cloud/index.md): Managed vs. unmanaged cluster connections, one Operator per cluster, kubeconfig and context management, MeshSync deployment modes, and cloud-specific guidance for operating Meshery across many clusters and clouds.
- [Monitoring, Observability & Health KPIs](/installation/production/monitoring-observability-and-kpis/index.md): Health endpoints, the key performance indicators of Meshery's health, metrics, distributed tracing, centralized logging, alerting, and synthetic checks for observing Meshery in production.
- [Operational Readiness Checklist & Known Caveats](/installation/production/operational-readiness-checklist/index.md): A consolidated, actionable production-readiness checklist across every dimension, the upgrade strategy for Meshery, and the known caveats and limitations to plan around.
- [Accessing Meshery UI](/installation/accessing-meshery-ui/index.md): Accessing Meshery's web-based user interface
- [Air-Gapped Installation](/installation/kubernetes/air-gapped/index.md): Install Meshery on Kubernetes in an air-gapped (offline) environment using Helm, a private registry, or side-loaded images.
- [AKS](/installation/kubernetes/aks/index.md): Manage your AKS clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in AKS in-cluster or out-of-cluster.
- [Bash](/installation/mesheryctl/linux-mac/bash/index.md): Install Meshery CLI on Linux or MacOS with Bash
- [Brew](/installation/mesheryctl/linux-mac/brew/index.md): Install Meshery CLI on Linux or macOS with Homebrew
- [Codespaces](/installation/advanced/codespaces/index.md): Build and contribute to Meshery using GitHub Codespaces
- [DigitalOcean](/installation/kubernetes/digitalocean/index.md): Install Meshery on DigitalOcean. Deploy Meshery out-of-cluster with Docker on a Droplet, or in-cluster on DigitalOcean Kubernetes (DOKS).
- [Docker Extension](/installation/docker/docker-extension/index.md): Install Docker Extension for Meshery
- [EKS](/installation/kubernetes/eks/index.md): Install Meshery on Elastic Kubernetes Service. Deploy Meshery in EKS in-cluster or outside of EKS out-of-cluster.
- [GKE](/installation/kubernetes/gke/index.md): Install Meshery on Google Kubernetes Engine. Deploy Meshery in GKE in-cluster or outside of GKE out-of-cluster.
- [Helm](/installation/kubernetes/helm/index.md): Install Meshery on Kubernetes using Helm. Deploy Meshery in Kubernetes in-cluster.
- [KinD](/installation/kubernetes/kind/index.md): Install Meshery on KinD. Deploy Meshery in KinD in-cluster or outside of KinD out-of-cluster.
- [KubeSphere](/installation/kubernetes/kubesphere/index.md): Install Meshery on KubeSphere
- [Minikube](/installation/kubernetes/minikube/index.md): Install Meshery on Minikube. Deploy Meshery in Minikube in-cluster or outside of Minikube out-of-cluster.
- [Scoop](/installation/mesheryctl/windows/scoop/index.md): Install Meshery CLI on Windows with Scoop
- [Server Environment Variables](/installation/advanced/environment-variables/index.md): Installation and runtime configuration reference for the environment variables consumed by Meshery Server.
- [Using Multiple Adapters](/installation/advanced/multiple-adapters/index.md): Choose which Meshery Adapters to run, run more than one instance of an adapter, or run none at all.

## Concepts
- [Concepts](/concepts/index.md): Concepts for understanding Meshery's various features and components.

- [Adapters](/concepts/architecture/adapters/index.md): Adapters extend Meshery's management capabilities in any number of ways, including lifecycle, configuration, performance, governance, identity...
- [Broker](/concepts/architecture/broker/index.md): Meshery broker component facilitates data streaming between kubernetes cluster components and outside world.
- [Catalog](/concepts/architecture/catalog/index.md): Browsing and using cloud native patterns
- [Components](/concepts/logical/components/index.md): Meshery Components identify and characterize infrastructure under management.
- [Connections](/concepts/logical/connections/index.md): Meshery Connections are managed and unmanaged resources that either through discovery or manual entry are managed by a state machine and used within one or more Environments.
- [Credentials](/concepts/logical/credentials/index.md): Meshery uses one or more Credentials when authenticating to a managed or unmanaged Connection.
- [Database](/concepts/architecture/database/index.md): Meshery offers support for internal caching with the help of file databases. This has been implemented with several libraries that supports different kinds of data formats.
- [Deployment Engine](/concepts/architecture/deployment-engine/index.md): How Meshery fulfills a design - resolving the registrant behind each component and routing that component either to Meshery Server itself or to a Meshery Adapter.
- [Designs](/concepts/logical/designs/index.md): Meshery Designs are descriptive, declarative characterizations of how your Kubernetes infrastructure should be configured.
- [Environments](/concepts/logical/environments/index.md): Environments are how you organize your deployment targets (whether on-premises servers or cloud services) into resource groups.
- [MeshSync](/concepts/architecture/meshsync/index.md): MeshSync ensures Meshery Server is continuously in-sync with the state of infrastructure under management.
- [Models](/concepts/logical/models/index.md): Meshery uses a set of resource models to define concrete boundaries to ensure extensible and sustainable management.
- [Operator](/concepts/architecture/operator/index.md): Meshery Operator controls and manages the lifecycle of components deployed inside a kubernetes cluster
- [Organizations](/concepts/logical/organizations/index.md): Organizations are the unit of tenancy in Meshery — they group users together and own all of the resources those users create.
- [Patterns](/concepts/logical/patterns/index.md): Meshery Patterns are descriptive, declarative characterizations of how your Kubernetes infrastructure should be configured.
- [Policies](/concepts/logical/policies/index.md): Meshery Policies enable you with a broad set of controls and governance of the behavior of systems under Meshery's management.
- [Registry](/concepts/logical/registry/index.md): Meshery Registry is a database acting as the central repository for all capabilities known to Meshery. These capabilities encompass various entities, including models, components, relationships, and policies.
- [Relationships](/concepts/logical/relationships/index.md): Meshery Relationships identify and facilitate genealogy between Components.
- [Workspaces](/concepts/logical/workspaces/index.md): Meshery Workspaces act as central collaboration point for teams.

## Guides
- [Guides](/guides/index.md): Using, operating, and troubleshooting Meshery.

- [Overview](/guides/infrastructure-management/overview/index.md): Meshery provides the ability to manage infrastructure for agility, maintainability, diversity, reliability and isolation, security, and speed.
- [Registering a Connection](/guides/infrastructure-management/registering-a-connection/index.md): Use the Connection Wizard to create and update Connections - Kubernetes clusters, Grafana, Prometheus, and more - in your Meshery deployment.
- [Configuring Meshery Operator, MeshSync, and Broker](/guides/infrastructure-management/configuring-operator-meshsync-broker/index.md): Tune how Meshery deploys and operates Meshery Operator, MeshSync, and Meshery Broker on your clusters - deployment modes, discovery scope, secret handling, service networking, and the behavioral impact of every setting.
- [Bringing Existing Infrastructure Under Meshery Management](/guides/infrastructure-management/managing-existing-infrastructure/index.md): What happens when you point Meshery at a cluster that is already running workloads - how brownfield discovery works, what to evaluate before you connect, the end-to-end process, and the caveats.
- [Deploying a Design](/guides/infrastructure-management/deploying-a-design/index.md): Validate, dry-run, deploy, and undeploy a Meshery Design on the Kubernetes clusters in your Environments, and read the deployment results.
- [Sharing a Cluster with Your Team](/guides/infrastructure-management/sharing-a-cluster-with-your-team/index.md): Give your teammates access to a Kubernetes cluster you manage in Meshery by grouping it into an Environment, attaching the Environment to a Workspace, and assigning teams to the Workspace.
- [Kubernetes Connection Lifecycle](/guides/infrastructure-management/kubernetes-connection-lifecycle/index.md): What happens end-to-end when Meshery manages a Kubernetes cluster - the connection states, the in-cluster components (Operator, Broker/NATS, MeshSync), MeshSync deployment modes, how Meshery reaches and authenticates to the Broker, the built-in Diagnostics, and how to operate and troubleshoot it all.
- [Grafana Dashboards](/guides/telemetry/grafana-dashboards/index.md): Browse, pin, and render your existing Grafana dashboards inside Meshery using a registered Grafana connection.
- [Prometheus Metrics](/guides/telemetry/prometheus-metrics/index.md): Explore Prometheus metrics, compose PromQL queries with live preview, and save your own panels - all from a registered Prometheus connection.
- [Authenticating Meshery via CLI](/guides/mesheryctl/authenticate-with-meshery-via-cli/index.md): Log in to Meshery Server from mesheryctl and get an authentication token.
- [Configuring Autocompletion for `mesheryctl`](/guides/mesheryctl/configuring-autocompletion-for-mesheryctl/index.md): Bash, Zsh, Oh My Zsh, and fish autocompletion for `mesheryctl` commands.
- [Create Models](/guides/configuration-management/creating-models/index.md): A comprehensive guide on creating models in Meshery, covering both CLI and UI methods.
- [Creating a Meshery Design](/guides/configuration-management/creating-a-meshery-design/index.md): Learn how to create a Meshery Design using the built-in Design Configurator in Meshery UI or the mesheryctl CLI.
- [Deploy AWS EC2 Instances with Meshery](/guides/tutorials/aws/deploy-aws-ec2-instances-with-meshery/index.md): Deploy an EC2 instance and its VPC from Meshery, using AWS Controllers for Kubernetes (ACK) and designs from the Meshery Catalog.
- [Deploy Azure resources with Meshery](/guides/tutorials/azure/deploy-azure-resources-with-meshery/index.md): Install Azure Service Operator in your cluster and deploy Azure resources, such as Storage Accounts and Key Vaults, from a Meshery Design.
- [Deploy Azure Storage Account with Meshery](/guides/tutorials/azure/deploy-azure-storage-account-with-meshery/index.md): Install Azure Service Operator in your cluster and deploy an Azure Storage Account from a Meshery Design.
- [Edge Styles Guide](/guides/configuration-management/edges-guide/index.md): Learn about the different edge styles and how to interpret their visual meaning in Meshery's component relationships.
- [Embedding a Meshery Design in a WordPress Post](/guides/tutorials/wordpress/embedding-meshery-design-in-wordpress/index.md): Embed an interactive Meshery Design in a WordPress post, using the embed export from Kanvas.
- [Envoy WASM Filter Management](/guides/infrastructure-management/filter-management/index.md): Import, inspect, publish, and remove Envoy WebAssembly (WASM) filters with Meshery UI and mesheryctl.
- [Exporting Models](/guides/configuration-management/exporting-models/index.md): Export a Meshery Model as an OCI image or a compressed archive.
- [GitOps with Meshery](/guides/infrastructure-management/gitops-with-meshery/index.md): Add Meshery's GitHub Actions to your pipelines to render a visual snapshot of your infrastructure on each pull request and to catch performance regressions before you merge.
- [Identifying Meshery Components](/guides/configuration-management/identifying-components/index.md): A guide to help you identify and understand the various component icons, shapes, and visual styles used across the Meshery UI.
- [Importing and Exporting Designs](/guides/configuration-management/import-export-designs/index.md): Manage and transfer Meshery designs seamlessly through import and export using CLI and UI.
- [Importing Models](/guides/configuration-management/importing-models/index.md): Import an existing Meshery Model into Meshery's registry from a file, a directory, a URL, or CSV files.
- [Interpreting Performance Test Results](/guides/performance-management/interpreting-performance-test-results/index.md): Read the latency and throughput results of a Meshery performance test, and compare runs in a way that produces useful conclusions.
- [Managing Connections](/guides/infrastructure-management/lifecycle-management/index.md): Find, inspect, transition, reconfigure, and remove the Connections Meshery manages, from Meshery UI or mesheryctl.
- [Managing Events with Notification Center](/guides/infrastructure-management/notification-management/index.md): Meshery tracks operations performed on your infrastructure and workloads, and provides notification of environment issues, application conflicts with infrastructure configuration, policy violations, and so on.
- [Managing Performance](/guides/performance-management/managing-performance/index.md): Organize load tests into performance profiles, choose and configure the load generator, and read infrastructure metrics alongside your results.
- [Meshery Operator, MeshSync, Broker Troubleshooting Guide](/guides/troubleshooting/meshery-operator-meshsync/index.md): Comprehensive guidance for troubleshooting Meshery Operator, MeshSync and Broker deployments under various scenarios.
- [Mesheryctl system commands](/guides/mesheryctl/system-commands/index.md): Use mesheryctl system commands to start, stop, update, and inspect your Meshery deployments.
- [Performance Management with Meshery](/guides/performance-management/performance-management/index.md): Run a load test against a service endpoint from Meshery UI, mesheryctl, or a CI pipeline, save it as a reusable performance profile, and compare results over time.
- [Publishing Meshery Designs to Artifact Hub](/guides/tutorials/artifacthub/publish-to-artifacthub/index.md): Export a Meshery Design as an OCI image and publish it to an Artifact Hub repository.
- [Push or Pull a Model Image](/guides/configuration-management/push-pull-model-image/index.md): Push or pull a model image to or from an OCI-compatible image repository.
- [Running mesheryctl in a CI Pipeline](/guides/mesheryctl/running-mesheryctl-in-ci/index.md): Install mesheryctl on a CI runner, authenticate it without a browser, point it at a Meshery Server, and run commands non-interactively.
- [Running system checks using Meshery CLI](/guides/mesheryctl/running-system-checks-using-mesheryctl/index.md): Run pre-flight and post-deployment system health checks using Meshery's CLI, mesheryctl.
- [Troubleshooting Errors while running Meshery](/guides/troubleshooting/meshery-server/index.md): Troubleshoot errors from mesheryctl system start and from running Meshery Server locally with make server.
- [Troubleshooting Extensions for Local Development](/guides/troubleshooting/enabling-extensions-locally/index.md): Find out why a Meshery extension doesn't load in your local development environment, and what you can fix yourself.
- [Troubleshooting Meshery Installations](/guides/troubleshooting/installation/index.md): Troubleshoot Meshery installation and deployment
- [Using Meshery CLI](/guides/mesheryctl/working-with-mesheryctl/index.md): Guides for common tasks while using Meshery's CLI, mesheryctl.
- [Using Metrics in Meshery](/guides/performance-management/meshery-metrics/index.md): How to view Prometheus and Grafana metrics in Meshery

## Contributing and Community
- [Contributing and Community](/project/index.md): Information about contributing to the Meshery project and participating the Meshery community.

- [Contributing to Models Quick Start](/project/contributing/models/contributing-models-quick-start/index.md): A no-fluff guide to creating your own Meshery Models quickly.
- [Contributing to Models](/project/contributing/models/models/index.md): How to contribute to Meshery Models, Components, Relationships, Policies...
- [Contributing to Components](/project/contributing/models/components/index.md): How to contribute to Meshery Model Components
- [Contributing to Connections](/project/contributing/models/connections/index.md): How to define a new Connection and register it so Meshery understands it and includes it in the Connection Wizard.
- [Contributing to Relationships](/project/contributing/models/relationships/index.md): How to contribute to Meshery Models Relationships, Policies...
- [Contributing to Operator, MeshSync & Broker Settings](/project/contributing/contributing-controllers-config/index.md): The complete surface of settings that govern Meshery Operator, MeshSync and Meshery Broker behavior: where each one lives, what it writes, what reads it, and what happens when it changes.

- [Frequently Asked Questions](/project/faq/index.md): General commonly asked questions and answers about Meshery.

- [Extensibility: APIs](/reference/extensibility/api/index.md): Meshery architecture is extensible, offering an array of extension points and REST and GraphQL APIs.
- [Extensibility: Authorization](/reference/extensibility/authorization/index.md): Meshery architecture is extensible. Meshery provides several extension points for working with different cloud native projects via authorization, adapters, load generators and providers.
- [Extensibility: Build-time](/reference/extensibility/build-time/index.md): System integrators can supply build-time configuration, data, packages, and other extensions to Meshery's container image.
- [Extensibility: Load Generators](/reference/extensibility/load-generators/index.md): Meshery offers support for more types of Kubernetes and cloud native infrastructure than any other project or product in the world. Meshery uses adapters for more deeply managing specific types of infrastructure.
- [Extensibility: Providers](/reference/extensibility/providers/index.md): Meshery uses providers to enrich the level of depth by which it manages cloud native infrastructure.
- [Extensibility: Schemas](/reference/extensibility/schemas/index.md): Meshery schemas support x-* vendor extensions as an intentional extensibility mechanism for remote providers to attach provider-specific metadata.
- [Extensibility: UI](/reference/extensibility/ui/index.md): Meshery offers support for more adapters than any other project or product in the world. Meshery UI has a number of extension points that allow users to customize their experience with third-party plugins.
- [GraphQL API Reference](/reference/graphql-apis/index.md): Meshery GraphQL API Documentation and Reference
- [Meshery Operator CRDs](/reference/meshery-operator-crds/index.md): Details of the Custom Resource Definitions included in Meshery Operator and used by its custom controllers.
